points.t: A red, swollen, tender nail fold: **hours–days** (acute) or **weeks–months with a lost cuticle** (chronic).
Acute: *S. aureus* / strep after minor trauma. Chronic: **wet work** breaks the cuticle seal; *Candida* passenger or driver.
Acute: **warm soaks**, drain pus, antibiotic only if spreading. Chronic: **keep dry**, cotton-under-rubber gloves, potent steroid ± azole.
**Herpetic whitlow** (don’t incise), tendon-sheath infection, and **nail-unit melanoma or SCC** posing as paronychia.

cause.lead: The cuticle is a seal; break it and the fold fills.
points: **Acute** (< 6 weeks): *S. aureus*, streptococci, sometimes *Pseudomonas*; or HSV (whitlow).
**Chronic** (> 6 weeks): irritant dermatitis of the fold + secondary **Candida** (± Gram-negatives).
Triggers: **wet work**, cold hands, manicures, cuticle picking; hairdressers, cleaners, bar and food workers.
Host: hand dermatitis, diabetes, immunosuppression, poor circulation.

features.lead: Tempo and number of digits tell them apart.
points: **Chronic**: swollen tender proximal folds, **lost cuticle**, fold lifted off plate, intermittent discharge.
Nail: **transverse ridging**, discolouration, onycholysis near the fold; several digits over time.

visuals.caption: Acute paronychia (left): one hot swollen lateral fold with a pus pocket. Chronic paronychia (right): puffy proximal fold, missing cuticle and ridged nail.
visuals.alt: Fingertips with acute and chronic paronychia

items.name: Cuticle loss
items.t: Lifted fold: a portal for yeast.

items.name: Candidal nail
items.t: Plate change starting near the cuticle.

points: History of wet work + lost cuticle = chronic.
Bacterial swab if acute abscess; **viral swab** if grouped vesicles.
Candida in a dystrophic nail without fold disease may be secondary.

cards.name: Dermatophyte onychomycosis
cards.clue: Starts distal / lateral; toenails; tinea pedis.

manage.lead: Acute: drain. Chronic: fix the environment.

points: Keep hands **dry and warm**; **cotton-lined waterproof gloves**; no cuticle cutting; emollient barrier.
Potent topical steroid to the fold ± topical azole (CKS), weeks–months.
**Warm (± saline) soaks 3–4 times a day, 10–15 min**; dry between; elevate; analgesia. Most settle without antibiotics.
**Incision and drainage** (or lift the eponychium); partial nail removal if pus under the plate.

rx.drug: Flucloxacillin (only if spreading, unwell, diabetic or immunocompromised)

points: Oral **itraconazole** or fluconazole (not terbinafine); check CYP3A4 interactions.

visuals.caption: Wet-work protection: a thin cotton glove under a rubber glove keeps the nail folds dry. Change when damp.
visuals.alt: Cotton glove under a rubber glove at a sink

items.t: **Kanavel signs** (flexor tenosynovitis), **felon**, spreading cellulitis, fever: surgical assessment.
Diabetes, PAD or immunosuppression with a toe infection.
Single nail with persistent ‘paronychia’, destruction or pigment: exclude **melanoma / SCC**.

pearls.t: Treat the **fold environment**, not only the tablet.
Chronic paronychia isn’t a strep or Pseudomonas infection.
Terbinafine is poorly active against yeasts: use an azole for Candida.

quiz.q: Grouped vesicles on a painful fingertip?

quiz.a: Flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily for 5–7 days.
Wet work and irritant damage to the cuticle, with secondary Candida.
